title: Clarinet players he admired
summary: He names Willie Humphrey and other clarinetists he heard and worked with.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Who were the outstanding, say, clarinet players when you were here for writing music?

The one that impressed me most was Willie Humphrey. I saw him in the street parades, when I had a little E flat. You have the piercing sound over those brass bands, you know, really wailing on the horn.

Willie Humphrey, the one that's working with Paul now. Earl Humphrey's brother. He impressed me, but he lived uptown and never had a chance much to him. And he's the one that impressed me, I thought he was a master. There were others, like Big Al Lloyd, who was always in the same track in the summer of retirement. He played if he got a chance. I worked with him, I know him at Twy, and Walter DeCoult, four of us at the Bungalow. Out on the Shellback Road, I worked a couple of months out there with them. He was real great in the style, and I was Piku, was great. And all the real wildcats at the left, like Jim and Noom, John of Dodge, Bonnie de Gat was around, he and Alvin Nichols, but they weren't teaching kinds of old, teaching the taxiderms.
